messages.author: 1667ac6354bdba89
messages.subject: updateSelectInput based on another updateSelectInput - can't get it to work
parts:
Hello, I wondered if anyone would be able to help me with my frustration in trying to creating some "cascading" menu options for my app.

I'd like to be able to change options on menu's based on what has been selected from previous menus, i.e.

User chooses option A from menu1, menu2 displays A1,A2,A3.
User chooses option B from menu1, menu2 displays B1,B2,B3
etc.

I'd eventually like to have 3 layers of menu, then use the options selected for further work.

I thought this would be simple given updateSelectInput() but  just can't get it working, and so I hope someone here could help with my frustrations :)

I have also tried with renderUI(), but then I don't see how I can select the input value from that to get the other menu's to update.

I've tried to create an example below, here is my code:

SERVER.R
==========

library(shiny)

## test dataframe
df <- data.frame(option1 = c("A","A","B","B","C","C"),
                 option2 = c("A1","A2","B3","B1","C2","C3"),
                 option3 = c(T,F,T,F,T,F),
                 option4 = c("a","b","c","d","e","f"))

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
 
  ## would like to be able to change the rows displayed here eventually
  output$table1 <- renderTable({
    df
  })
 
  ## for insight into what the menu vars are holding
  output$bugs <- renderText({
    text <- paste("menu1:", input$menu1,
                "menu2:", input$menu2,
                "menu3:", input$menu3)
  })
 
  ## expected behaviour - to show A, B or C
  ## actual - blank
  observe({
    if (is.null(input$menu1))
      return
   
    choice1 <- as.character(unique(df$option1))
#    names(choice1) <- 1:length(choice1)
   
    updateSelectInput(session,
                      "menu1",
                      choices = choice1)
  })
 
  ## expected behaviour - to show A1,B2,C etc based on what menu1 has chosen
  ## actual - doesn't update choices from default
  observe({
    if (length(input$menu1) < 2 )
      return()

    x <- input$menu1
   
    choice2 <- df[df$option1 == x,
                  "option2"]
    names(choice2) <- 1:length(choice2)
   
    updateSelectInput(session,
                      "menu2",
                      choices = choice2)
  })
 
  ## expected behaviour - to update choices based on menu3
  ## actual - no change
  observe({
    if (is.null(input$menu1) ||
          is.null(input$menu2) ||
          is.null(input$menu3)) ## these don't work, the input$menu's take the default list values
      return
   
    choice3 <- df[df$option1 == input$menu1 & df$option2 == input$menu2,
                  "option3"]
   
    updateSelectInput(session,
                      "menu1",
                      choices = choice3)
  })
 
  ## use these?
#   outputOptions(output, "menu1", priority = 1)
#   outputOptions(output, "menu2", priority = 2)
#   outputOptions(output, "menu3", priority = 3)
 
})


UI.R
====

library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
 
  # Application title
  headerPanel("Menu Test"),
 
  # Sidebar with a slider input for number of observations
  sidebarPanel(
    textOutput("bugs"), #showing the values of the menu options below
    selectInput("menu1",
                "Menu1",
                choices = list("default1") #default, I would like this value to update
    ),
    selectInput("menu2",
                "Menu2",
                choices = list("default2") #default, I would like this value to update
                ),
    selectInput("menu3",
                "Menu3",
                choices = list("default3") #default, I would like this value to update
                )

  ),

  mainPanel(
    tableOutput("table1")
  )
))

parts:
Hi all,

I'm struggling with a similar problem, but I can't get the solution.

I've got a couple of select fields which values depend on the selection of other input items.

Issues are two:
a) For one of the fields, the choices only get updated if I change one of the previous fields, but ignores changes on other.
b) The other field does not change at all.

I'll try to explain more graphically:
I've got 3 input fields: input$area, input$tab (both selectInput) and input$interval (dateRangeInput)

When I change any of them, I want that the values of input$links and input$users (both selectInputs created in the server side via renderUI) get updated.

What happens is:
a) input$links is only responsive to input$area and input$tab, but ignores changes on input$interval.
b) input$users is only updated when server is started.

Can you help me, please?

The code is this:
server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  linksChoices <- reactive({
    areaList <- input$areas
    tabList <- input$tabs
    input$interval
    interval1 <- input$interval[1]
    interval2 <- input$interval[2]
    getLinks(areaList, tabList, interval1, interval2) #This function returns the desired item list
  })
 
  userselect <- reactive({
    areaList <- input$areas
    tabList <- input$tabs
    linkList <- input$links
    interval1 <- input$interval[1]
    interval2 <- input$interval[2]
    getUsers(areaList, tabList, linkList, interval1, interval2) #This function returns the desired item list
  })
 
  #Create the selectInput input$links
  output$uiLink <- renderUI({
    input$areas
    input$tabs
    selectInput("links", "Select links",
                isolate(linksChoices()),
                multiple=TRUE,
                selectize=TRUE,
                width = "100%"
    )
  })
 
  #Create the selectInput input$users
  output$uiUser <- renderUI({
    selectInput("users", "User",
                isolate(userselect()),
                multiple=FALSE,
                selectize=TRUE,
                width = "100%"
    )
  })

It turns out it was the isolate clause the one that was stopping the update of the controls.
